data.narrative:
Skyeton is a growth-stage company in Defense & Security founded by Oleksandr Stepura. The valuation exercise draws from a comp universe of 10 private and public peers: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems. The Defense & Security sector contains 21 identifiable peers overall.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable to Skyeton's valuation. The dataset identified zero same-stage matches, zero adjacent-stage matches, and zero similar-tier comps within the narrow filter parameters—falling short of the three-datapoint minimum threshold for statistical reliability. A fallback to all-sector median multiples would introduce material bias given the heterogeneity of Defense & Security business models and margins. This constraint eliminates the most direct triangulation method.

Without applicable peer multiples, precedent transaction analysis, or disclosed financial metrics, a defensible valuation range cannot be established from the available data. The analysis indicates that standard public-market and narrowly-screened private-peer benchmarking are both insufficient to support a point estimate or range. Resolution would require either: (1) access to financial performance data (revenue, EBITDA) for the target and comp set, (2) expansion of the comp universe beyond strict stage/tier filters, or (3) alternative methods such as discounted cash flow if projections are available. The current dataset supports only the negative finding that peer-median methods are not yet viable.
